baer-heitev/1:_: When it arrives — likewise he should say so in prayer after completing prayer as a request. One may say the wickedness in haste — Beit Yosef. To make them forget Your Torah and remove them from Your statutes, etc., without memi"n — Shach, Mordechai, so Knesset HaGedolah. Bazman without vav — Taz, not like Levush who wrote uvezman hazeh with vav — end. One may say these eight days of Hanukkah are for thanks, etc. Magen Avraham:
chokhmat-shlomo/1:_: Seif 1 in Hagahah: some say when he forgot to say al hanissim, etc. NB: See Taz in tractate Berachot who challenged this — one should not pray for a miracle; we already wrote to resolve this in our novellae; see in darush for Hanukkah year 5559 to resolve another way: distinguish between a private miracle and a public miracle — only for an individual one may not rely on a miracle and request it; but to request for the community is permitted to rely on a miracle and request — end, in his reason it is good — examine.
eliyah-rabbah/3:_: [ג] [Levush] In order to include, etc. I say even with vav it means those miracles He did for our ancestors and bazman hazeh of this month (Levushei Yom Tov), and Taz agreed to say bazman without vav.
mishnah-berurah/1:ג: (ג) We do not return him — for they are not d'oraisa; it refers to prayer and Birkat HaMazon; there is no distinction in Birkat HaMazon between weekday and Shabbat of Hanukkah — even though he must eat because it is Shabbat, nevertheless he does not return for al hanissim of Hanukkah [Peri Megadim]; see siman 188 in Mishna Berurah end s.k. 133.
turei-zahav/3:_: As You did. It appears per this wording it should be "so You will do for us" — for per this it is prayer; this is the reason of the 11th who cannot say it because one does not request needs in the last three [within prayer]; since Beit Yosef concludes permission is in the pray-er's hand, if so what Rama wrote in seif 1 that in synagogue one says as You did, etc., and in synagogue in Nodeh Lecha it is thanks — nevertheless one may say so; all the more after prayer one may say as request "do for us miracles as You did," etc. In the wording al hanissim Levush wrote one may say bayamim hahem uvezman hazeh with vav to include all miracles for ancestors and to specify that miracle — now like the event — each day He does for us open and hidden miracles as for ancestors open and hidden — end; I do not think so, for then why bayamim hahem — certainly it was in those days when ancestors lived; granted for bazman without vav one must say so, otherwise it implies in bazman hazeh while we exist a miracle was done for ancestors — therefore must say bayamim hahem bazman hazeh as if saying in those days on such-and-such of the month; also one passing where a miracle occurred says Blessed is He who performed a miracle for me in this place — siman 218 — and did not say uvemakom hazeh to include other hidden miracles — that is not in the wording at all and erroneous to say uvezman with vav as I wrote.
yad-ephraim/2:_: Taz s.k. 5: in synagogue in Nodeh Lecha it is thanks, etc. — requires study, for Rama speaks when he forgot Nodeh Lecha and says in Harachaman which is request; if his intent: since his primary establishment is in Birkat HaMazon in Nodeh Lecha — why write nevertheless he may say so all the more in prayer, etc. — also in prayer primary is thanks — what preference over prayer?
